zh.domain: Same original ray in homogeneous parallel planar layers; no edge, roughness or scattering effects. Geometric propagating entry into air is distinguished from a grazing direction.

option_checks.evidence: Strict original TIR has K=N_water sin(alpha)>N_air. Parallel layers conserve K, so sin(gamma)=K/N_air>1 cannot describe a propagating air ray.
Large N_oil may permit an oil branch, but cannot change conserved K at the oil-air boundary; the final obstruction remains.

If N_oil<K reflection occurs first; if equal it is grazing; if greater the oil ray reaches a final TIR interface. None escapes into air. Original critical equality likewise gives only a grazing final direction, not entry with normal flux.
The no-escape conclusion depends on K relative to air, not a numerical oil index. The missing oil value changes the first-interface regime, not this conclusion.

Q7_visible_domain_counterexample.purpose: New diagnostic check of the displayed choice domain, not a re-solution or replacement of d493's frozen direct-route original solution. No image or source material-index data is invented.
Q7_visible_domain_counterexample.analytic_geometry: Equilateral triangle A=(0,0), B=(L,0), C=(L/2,sqrt(3)L/2), L>0. Entry P=(L/4,0) on AB. Internal normal ray u=(0,1) reaches T=(L/4,sqrt(3)L/4) on AC; reflection there gives direction (sqrt(3)/2,1/2). It exits BC at Q=(5L/8,3sqrt(3)L/8).
Q7_visible_domain_counterexample.equal_distance_check: BP=BQ=3L/4, positive and strictly within both adjacent faces meeting at B.
Q7_visible_domain_counterexample.normal_crossings: Entry is normal to AB. The reflected direction is the outward normal of BC, so exit is normal as well; both exterior angles are0, not grazing.
Q7_visible_domain_counterexample.third_face_reflection: Incidence at AC is60 degrees. For n/n_a>2, n sin(60 degrees)>n_a, so the one internal reflection is strict TIR. No coating or scattering is required.
Q7_visible_domain_counterexample.result: For arbitrarily large positive relative indices above2 this reflected ray actually enters, crosses and leaves at equal distances from B. Both displayed stems admit it. Hence all four finite-bound answers fail as statements of the entire currently displayed route domain.
